section.title: Modeling with differential equations
section.p: A derivative measures an instant-by-instant rate. A differential equation starts when a situation gives that rate before it gives the function.
The direction is different from many earlier problems. We are not given y(t) and asked to find y'(t). We are given information about y'(t) and asked to find y(t).

subsection.title: A law that gives a rate
subsection.p: A hot cup of coffee cools quickly when it is much hotter than the room. Later, when it is only a little warmer than the room, it cools slowly.
That observation is the heart of Newton’s law of cooling:

note.title: A differential equation
note.p: A differential equation is an equation involving an unknown function and one or more of its derivatives.

subsection.p: The equation does not yet tell us the temperature at every time. It tells us how the temperature should be changing once the temperature is known.
That is the new kind of problem.

exercise.title: What does it mean to write a law as a derivative?

statement.p: A differential equation specifies y' rather than y itself. In your own words, why is that a natural way to write a scientific law, and what extra information is needed before a unique solution is determined?

hint.p: Many laws say how a quantity is changing, not what its current value is. An initial condition picks one graph from a family.

subsection.title: Solution as an unknown function
subsection.p: A solution of a differential equation is a function that makes the equation true.
Start with a simpler equation:
This says that the rate of change of y depends on the current value of y.
If y is below 1, then 1-y>0, so the solution should rise.
If y is above 1, then 1-y<0, so the solution should fall.
If y=1, then 1-y=0, so the solution should stay flat.
Before solving the equation by a method, we can check proposed functions.

The same differential equation has many solutions. That should not be surprising. An antiderivative also comes with a constant C. A differential equation often gives a whole family of possible functions.

note.title: Solution of a differential equation
note.p: A function y(t) is a solution of a differential equation on an interval I if y is differentiable on I and the equation is true for every t in I.

statement.p: The interval matters. A formula may solve an equation on one interval but fail to make sense on another. This is the same domain discipline we used for logarithms, square roots, inverse trigonometric functions, and improper integrals.

subsection.title: Checking a proposed solution
subsection.p: Checking a solution is often easier than finding one. It is also one of the best ways to understand what the equation means.

note.title: How to check a proposed solution
note.p: To check a proposed solution of a differential equation:

li.p: State the interval where the function is being considered.
Substitute the function and its derivative into the differential equation.
Check that the equation is true for every point of the interval.
If there is an initial condition, check it separately.

note.title: A model check
note.p: A solution should satisfy the differential equation, the initial condition, and the behavior of the situation. Algebra alone is not enough if the model’s interpretation has been forgotten.

paragraphs.p: Many differential equations cannot be solved by guessing a familiar formula. But even without a formula, the equation still gives information. Since
tells the slope a solution must have at each point (t,y), we can draw those slopes. That picture is the next step.

exercise.title: Why is checking a proposed solution part of understanding the model?

statement.p: Checking a formula is often easier than finding one. In your own words, what should a complete check include besides differentiation and substitution, and why is algebra alone not enough if the interpretation has been forgotten?

hint.p: State the interval, check the differential equation, check any initial condition, and ask whether the long-term behavior matches the situation.
